first of all, it's worth noting that vampire requires third party patches to be an ideal experience. it doesn't like to work at all on modern operating systems and is buggy as hell even if you're on an older machine.
anyways, the first 25% of vampire is EXCELLENT and features some of my all time favorite quests in gaming history (ocean house is ♥♥♥♥ing timeless.) i've put a bit over 20 hours into this game, and more than half of that has probably been replaying the first chunk. the writing is generally witty and engaging, and no matter how you build your character you feel like you're doing SOMETHING right. the combat portions are weaker than exploring and talking to people, but they're usually not challenging enough to be particularly frustrating. they're usually just boring at worst. the problem is that after you leave the first area, the quality graaadually starts to dip downwards, and the game begins to forget what exactly made those first few hours so enjoyable.

the actually interesting stuff is slowly replaced with long, increasingly tough sections of combat, and combat is easily the worst part of the game. this also really ♥♥♥♥s you over if you skewed your character's stats to be more focused on charisma, because most combat is mandatory. this is in pretty stark contrast to the beginning of the game, where everything feels equally useful. instead, it's entirely possible for you to end up with a completely useless character past a certain point. the writing is still alright when it's actually there, but it's entirely absent for far longer stretches of the game than it should be. slowly trawling through a terrible sewer level with literally no relief isn't an ideal experience in any game, and it's an especially bad one in this. i would honestly say the last half or so of the game is barely worth playing, simply because the bad outweighs the good and the ending certainly isn't worth going through all of that♥♥♥♥♥♥ because the ending is terrible. it's really, really bad, dudes.
i would really love to recommend this game based on the merits of the first few hours, and it's entirely possible that you will manage to have a good time with the whole thing, but i can't. the experience is just too jumbled, the game is too buggy, and the combat is too much of a pain to deal with in excess. just watch a playthrough or something. there are great ideas here, they just wear thin.

I like roguelikes / -lites in all forms.
So no surprise this little gem is right down my alley.
The left-to-right scrolling concept is interesting, the hook is: you can only go forward, not backwards - the all-consuming darkness is always close and devours everything in it's path.
Since this game is technically turn-based and almost every action you can think of costs "time", you have to be on your toes even while shopping at one of the many procedurally generated villages / strongholds. More often than not, you will exit the settlement and hear the darkness consuming the NPCs you just chatted to or traded with.
You generate "Hero Points" during your travel to find the Demon Lord (the endboss), which you can use to unlock more character classes (you can unlock these while playing the game, as well), perks, and, most importantly, unlock/upgrade the "Dimensional Vault" - Here you can stash items the next character you play can profit from, such as a good weapon/armor, rare herbs and other gimmicks that make the playthrough easier.
The cute(ish) SNES JRPG-style graphics work very well, the soundtrack is excellent and atmospheric, and since this game is built around replayability, there is that, too.
The online portion is neglectable in my opinion, though there are some neat features such as your death/win message:
These get generated at the end and you can pick one from a quite big list, covering generic shout-outs (Like a boss!) to quite specific ones (My trusty Crescent Axe +5 helped me win!). You also meet the ghosts of dead players, which is nice since they even give you EXP boosts and sometimes more when you talk to them.
There are many more features and "featurettes", I won't go into detail, but as with any good roguelike, there is way more to it than meets the eye.
To name just a few: Underlying storyline with meetable / hirable plot characters, a companion system, pets, extensive perk system (this actually kind of works in place of a character generation - you decide what buffs you give your hero), several difficulties...
Also, apparently a DLC/Expansion is planned (One Way Heroics+), but it is allegedly only readable in japanese at this time, but among other things, there is at least one new class planned.
So the game will likely be expanded in the near future.
All in all, I highly recommend this for everyone who likes rogue-style games, the price is very modest and you get quite some fun for your money.

It's a cool game whose controls can be surprising to some. They're very responsive and precise and they provide a very good feedback. Clearly one of the best controls I've experienced with a platform game.
The game is about discovering every map and solving puzzles. You can only move around and jump. The puzzles are well thought as they're straightforward and mixed with the gameplay itself, mostly in the form of platforming itself ; calculating your path as you go through obstacles or figuring out the best way to do something. And if you die, you start back at the last checkpoint you activated (you may activate them coming across them and they have no limit in how many times you can activate them) and it doesn't feel like an huge chore like it can be in so many other games. Even spawning back behind a boss room and having to cross it again actually feels fun (you can't kill the bosses as far as I know).
So, there are some rooms with bosses. Those bosses mostly don't move and will just throw many projectiles across the room, with clear patterns. The goal there is to calculate your path in that and mix it up with fading, moving and rigid platforms, stops and monsters avoidance to reach the next map, and while it's not hard, from all the challenges I've seen in games, those are amongst the most fair, fun and rewarding there is. Even jumping around in the regular maps is fun so that the controls are good and the map structures well thought.
There are secret rooms with small collectibles and those are also very well thought as they don't hint themselves to you with obvious cues and are very well hidden but placed in a way that it will tickle your senses and make you find them or understand that they're there and it's very rare in recent games, and it's yet another feature that's rewarding by itself , as just finding them is fun and what's behind is a bonus, and adds to the fun overall.
From what I've seen you win the game upon doing 100% completion. You earn completion bits by bits by discovering maps and finding some unlocks providing new powers, allowing you to reach new places.
There is little story except hipsterish drawings on some of the walls. There is a small ambience that some would like and others not as you're pretty much alone in that word, always trying to solve puzzles and backtracking in order to find new places. The graphics are decent considering the theme they're set in, and are made neat to suit a certain comfort while playing.
I eventually got a bit bored with the backtracking and quit the game with 75% completion with a single character. Moving the character around and solving things was cool but at some point there was too much backtracking with little clues of how going forward and going back everywhere got tedious.
Now for a free game it's pretty well done and doesn't need to shy against many, many other games requiering a money purchase. There is no in-game microtransactions and no dlc, the game is standalone. And while some might find the game empty with the unique goal of doing 100% completion, linear progression and no npc interactions and little eye candy things, it has a solid and fun gameplay with very well done controls and it's worth trying out.

The game is really captivating in its own apocalyptic kind of way.  You are Brad,  A man that went through hell growing up with an abusive father, a sister that died, kids that beat him up.  Eventually he became older and started taking JOY (a highly addicted drug).  The Apocalypse happens and Brad finds a baby and names her Buddy.  He stops taking JOY.  Buddy grows up and eventually outsiders find her, unfortunately before this you learn she is the only female left on the planet.  Brad doesnt want anyone to hurt Buddy so this is where his journey begins.
The game and story is nothing short of Amazing.  For a 2D game that was made with Rpg Maker this was a bit of a shock how good this game came out.
Its not your typical game:  Through your journey you will come across people that want to harm you, kill you, take your things and blame you for not letting the girl re-establish humanity.  You make companions along the way (30 in all) that you meet during game.  Some you need to persuade, pay, threaten, blackmail, take hostages, save, work for, etc to get them to join their party.  There are tons of hidden secrets within this game.   Instead of constant battles happening at random you are treated to fight enemies where they are located, depending on the story events take place at different times but fights are never random.  Example: You may have a guy hiding behind a wall ready to attack you, someone that looks dead is actually not, someone friendly may want something from you at a random time.   So basically doing less fighting in the game gives you more to explore and story,  You will have to explore every area to fight random people and monsters to get your levels up, its more fun than it sounds.  There are major decisions in this game as well, would you rather save a new companions life or will harm yourself to save them?   Things are not what they seem either in this game, who is the bad guy in this story?  Is it you or is it someone else..? These are not easy things to figure out.
I do not think I have had this much fun in quite awhile with a game.  Very glad I tried this out when a sale happened, although now that I know how fantastic it was I would have gladly paid full price.
I really hope these games keep getting made and a franchise eventually comes about it for the Developer.  Fantastic work,The best Indie buy I have ever played on steam!

Say, you are an "Indie Game developer". You use a free stock game maker software. The first game you made received slight recognition, so what do you do? Make your own game engine and try to actually learn how to make a game properly? Hahaha, No! You make a kickstarter and ask for free money to do the same thing you did 10 years before. You just make a game that is mechanically even less advanced than your last one, cut off a little content and sell that almost a year later after your initial launch! LISA biggest problem aside from it's very "developer" might just be it's inmarketable Name. It tells you nothing about what this game is, what you can expect, play or what it is about. Which is probably why LISA bit the dust in comparision to the spergehttilordfest that became the Insufferable entity known as Undertale.
I had to pick my poison and so I went for this. This did not mean i enjoyed it however, it was just the lesser of 2 evils. In this game you take control of a man that could just be Jet Black from Cowboy Bebop thrown into a setting similar to Fist of the North Star. Except everybody is a sodomite and/or addicted to a mutagenic form of heroin. The prologue of the game in itself was as overstretched as it felt like a chore.
LISA tries very hard to be a tearjerker. It did little to nothing for me in that regard except acting overly pretentious trying to make me feel sorry for 16 bit stickmen. You are supposed to make "emotionally deep, meaningful" decision (which are little to none make in general with small or similar impact on the story, whether or not you actually do something or not). The most important part may just be if you are willing to get your arms amputated. Don't.
The protagonist adoptive child is a massive♥♥♥♥♥♥ For all I care he would have went better off to throw her off a cliff or feed her to wolves the second he found her. She act as much as an ungrateful ♥♥♥♥♥ as inhumanly possible and does nothing but cause trouble, pain and death upon her surroundings.
LISA gameplay has little going for it. A pokemon game from 1996 was more immersive. Even Cthulhu saves the world (which you can get on steam for 2 dollars) felt to me more complex than this ever could. It breaks down to finding the few overpowered team member to cheat out the shallow combat system. Once you have the oil and fire combo going your are set for the pity rest of the game. Except when you feel like collecting useless party members and find the few scattered secrets in the game that do little to nothing for the main Quest progression except XP.
The graphics are dull. for the most part. The level design looks all the same in all level, only varying in color for the most part. The sprite work deserves an honorable mention. The characters look mostly unique and represent the feel of a post apocalyptic world full of wacky murderous weirdos accurately. Same goes for the sound design. It's not outstanding, but it does it Job. Thats all good I can really say about it. If you are into wrestling and old Simpsons you will maybe get some joke references.
Id' like to say the developer tried the best he could. But that would be a lie. This project was a lazy attempt from the start and you are left with a semilinear game that plays each battle of identically after a certain point once you turned into a snowball. The end is as unsatisfying as the beginning. The only thing it did for me was feeling like the game was missing act IV. But i guess Jorgensen saved that for the DLC.
Which you can buy for 5 dollars. Don't do it. Not only is It overpriced. it is imbalanced. It's only excuse is an attempt to tie up the lose unexplained end of the stories with a combat system that focuses single handedly on a timed twitch of the finger. If you thought the combat system in the main game was repetitive, you don't want to experience this. You have 1 (read) one character at all times, with the exception of having a clone of the former main character for a short time. It's short. It's dumb. It's unjustly hard. I did it though but there was little pay off for having a beneficial numbers on the RNG generator.
All and All i can say is, LISA: The Painful RPG fails on the delivery. It is overpriced for what it offers. I expected nothing and still got disappointed by running and jumping through the same screen for 40 hours, pressing the same buttons. I doubt I will ever play this again. It felt like a cheap cash in for some guy who desperately needed money and I feel regret for falling into his trap. It takes a certain kind of ruthless audacity to charge money for a supposed royalty free RPG maker game. Never again.
Oh and thank you for the flipped bird you gave to your customers Dingaling. Twice. After a Metal Gear 3 ladder. I will not forget that.

There's a few points where you will quite likely die A LOT, but checkpoints are frequent and well-placed so you never lost more than 30 seonds' prograss, keeping even more frustrating segments from breaking the flow of the game.
Personally I would recommend playing this on a controller with the sensitivity on 1.5 because I found it to be a bit easier to manage the controls that way- there's not much to control, but the XInput mapping is simple and intuitive.
Overall A Story About My Uncle was a wonderful game- exactly as long as it should have been, a fun gameplay "hook", and fantastic execution in terms of technical performance and level design.

You are Vito Scaletta, Italian war hero who gets saved from the horrors of war by childhood friend and mafioso Joe Barbaro. From that point on, with Joe by your side, you are thrust into a tangled web of Empire baby, divided between three families. Fans of Goodfellas, the Godfather, or any 1940s-50s era gangsters will feel right at home. The game is divided up into "chapter" segments, which can be replayed at any time.
The game engine (while having some hilarious physics glitches) is smooth and beyond optimized. The facial texturing and animation excels at times and falls short at others. Let it also be known that there is no animation for walking up and down stairs, something you spend a surprising amount of time doing. However, to make up for it, the game possesses beautiful fabric physics that can be experienced simply by buying a coat. NVidia card owners with PhysX will appreciate 2K's efforts.
Perfect voice acting, realistic cars and gunfire, more songs from the era in the radio stations than in Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas
, and a stunning orchestral score with a single haunting melody that will visit you both in the game's menu and the game's stunning (albeit mysterious) ending.
Aside from lockpicking and some other interludes, nothing sets the gameplay apart from GTA in terms of driving and a third-person shooter. The game does include a speed limiter on the cars, which locks your highest possible speed at the speed limit, since the cops in this game are actually smart (in a sense) and come after you for speeding. You can also customize any car you procure, including changing the plates.
The vintage Playboy pinups the game uses as collectables add much to the playtime, but the game has no real freeroam. It can be modded in, as the glorious PC Master Race allows, but it does not come available out of the box.

Almost a perfect game but ultimately falls short because of a few glaring issues.
Mafia 2 has the best atmosphere of any game I have played. You play as a gangster in the 1940s-1950s and you feel like you are in the world. Everything about the cars, buildings, stores, and even the radio convinces you that you really are in that city. When you drive around and hear about the remote control being invented or see more powerful and modern cars as time progresses. The attention to detail is very nice with the speedometer being time correct, the radio tuning in on actual music from that era, and the cars being♥♥♥♥♥♥to handle and not going very fast. I have a HD 4000 and I can only run the game on the lowest settings but it still looks good enough to soak in the atmosphere
The story of the game revolves the typical mafia story of a guy who "started from the bottom" and grew his way up until he did something that made him realize that crime never plays. Its cliché but it’s a very good story here. The characters in this game feel real with you feel emotionally invested in your character hoping they make the choices you do.
The mechanics are OK with standard 3rd person shooter stuff. The game relies a lot on realism so you die faster. There is regenerating health but each time it recovers to a lower degree. There are stealth mechanics but you utilize them in maybe 2-3 missions depending on how you count them so they are kind of worthless. You get cool time period weapons with the classic Tommy being the weapon you rely on the most. You almost never have to buy any because you just pick them off the dead guys in missions with shooting. You have to use cover in the game and it feels fluid except when you want to go into covers along walls because Vito can’t figure out which wall (of a corner) to stick to.
A MAJOR issue with the game is that the sandbox is a lie (sort of). There is a large map where you can go and explore but 1) there isn’t anything to do and 2) there is no free roam. Normally, in sandbox games, you explore the world until you choose to start a mission but here, the moment you wake up, you have a mission to do. You can (in certain levels) go out and explore but the problem is that there isn’t anything you can do with that exploration except soak in the atmosphere. There are no side activities and two guys you meet who can give you work never have work for you. You can rob stores but all that happens is that it gives you money. The missions are all linear and they have zones which limit you. Mostly you just drive through the city doing... nothing. There is a mission where you are wanted and you have to get home without being spotted and that is where the city comes alive. With you having to create your own path through a live city trying to avoid the cops. But most of the levels is simply go here, shoot this, go here, shoot this, and drive home, sleep, and repeat. Also, there isn’t a free play mode at the end so you can’t experience the city without the missions.
The story also seemed rushed at the end. There were a lot of betrayals and twists and at the end I was like, "that’s it?" It honestly left me disappointed because the story had been pretty god so far. Speaking of the story, it kind of renders the point of money useless. You use the money to buy clothes and... More clothes but halfway through, you lose all that and you start over... Kind of renders the point of money useless.
In other matters, the cars handle like♥♥♥♥♥♥but that’s probably on purpose. The police are more real meaning that you can hit something and not raise your wanted level if a cop doesn't see you but they are kind of stupid because you can rob a store, steal clothes from the store and walk out without them recognizing you. The character animation is good but they look really plasticy. The camera has trouble in narrow spaces and I only had one bug.
Overall, it’s still a good game. Good mechanics and atmosphere but it lacks in execution and flutters out in the end. I still think it’s a good game but it could have been an amazing game.

I think that this game has been getting unfair negative reviews. I'll admit that my main thematic interests reside in WWII and 40s era material, as well as how the mobster genre has gained my attention as well. However, that did not influence my positive position on this game.
Mafia II has been compared to the Gran Theft Auto series and Saints Row series, but does not seem to stack up against them. That is probably because the people that see the game that way are simply looking for a casual shoot-em-up game where you get into ridiculous scenarios. Mafia II is not so much a shooter (although there is a considerable amount of gunplay), but more of a simulator. The way that the story is structured is meant to show the player what it might be like to work your way up from the bottom to higher tiers within the Italian mob. I read a few of the negative reviews, all of which complain about "boring, pointless missions" like the infamous "stacking crates" and courier missions. However, they failed to note that the purpose of these jobs are to show that the protagonist was faced with the choice of working legit jobs and earning very little, or doing risky, illegal things to earn more, quicker.
There are some fun little details that they put into the game that I cannot help but feel a bit enthralled about. Nothing really important, but more like the ability to open and close the hood/trunk of your car, the police will cite you for speeding or driving recklessly, and general interaction with the environment (light switches, radios, faucets, etc). It should be noted that this is an older game, but it can stand with some of the modern RPGs in terms of playability. It may not have a sprawling and over-populated city like in GTA IV or V, but more like a population of GTA: Vice City.
As far as the game goes in terms of story, mechanics, and playability, I would have to give it an 8.5/10. If you have any interest in era based games or being a REAL gangster, this might be something you'll want to take a gander at.

Another instantly addicting game, Hack, Slash, Loot by developer David Williamson is a work of turn based martial art. Roguelike, you have to take every chance, try every door and kill every creature in your path. Incredibly fun to play, you don’t know who or what is in the next room, leaving you on the edge of your seat making Hack, Slash, Loot a go to game.
First starting the game you are given the option of a Human, Wizard or Archer, with continued gameplay you are able to unlock another 29 over time. Throughout the game you will encounter hordes of monsters, demons, zombies, and a manifold of other creatures to battle. Being turn based, you have to wait your turn, so be prepared to click frantically until your turn comes only to miss and do it again. With that being said its not all clicking, there is a deeper level of gameplay involved in Hack, Slash, Loot. This game involves a tactical insight and understanding beyond pointing and clicking. Each different quests embodies another set of skills and approach at the game. The possibilities are endless, mixing and matching of accessories and armor make every run different and add a new level of excitement and draw to the game.
There are dark places in the world inhabited by evil denizens. Places filled with danger and foreboding where no ordinary man would dare to journey. However, there are a few who are willing to risk death in the name of good, in the name of justice, in the name of… valuable loot! Depending on what quest you choose you are given a backstory to give you a sense of what your goal is in your adventure. Within each of the different quests you encounter various creatures and characters that have roles in the story, or provide dialog pertaining to whats at hand. While some quests are easier than others, each are sure to keep you on your toes.
Play for a few minutes or get more serious and sit down for a few hours, the more you play Hack, Slash, Loot the deeper you become involved. The retro appeal of this game really sells it the most, imagine Realm of the Mad God meets MS-DOS Dungeons and Dragons, imagine Final Fantasy Tactics meets Hammerwatch, imagine playing while watching the animated Lord Of The Rings, because thats what I did and now I love this game. You have a control panel in front of you while navigating your hero throughout each quest. To the left you have the status of your character displaying armor and stats. In the middle, a mini map that lights up as you explore each room, this also serves as a quick point and click to get you across the level faster. On the right, the description and status of each tile, chest, monster or whatever you hover the mouse over.
With only the life you are given to start you must find chests or overturn dead bodies in order to find scrolls or potions to boost your health as well as other stats at the same time. These scrolls and potions are critical to gameplay and make Hack, Slash, Loot almost impossible to play without them. With 32 different classes to choose from, 6 unique quests, and an endless mixture of armor, weaponry and gear makes Hack, Slash, Loot an instant classic and a must have for any indie gamer.
Graphics: 6/10
Playability: 7/10
Story: 9/10
Challenge: 8/10
Replay Value: 7/10
If you wish for a terrible version of Nethack, you may want to consider Hack, Slash, Loot

So, before I begin, I would like to thank Dingaling for providing a fresh and fun entry into the indie genre, one that has affected me and many others greatly, and hopefully will endure the test of time.
I feel that the first thing I should do is address the drawing of parallels between Undertale and LISA. These games may share quite a bit, but it is absolutely NOT worth comparing the two, as they share completely different themes and gameplay focuses. Undertale's focus is more on gathering friendships and the value of those friendships. Undertale likes to be fair(so long as you are going pacifist), and will reward you for playing along. LISA is a take on how everything can be taken away from us in the blink of an eye, even if you DO play along. Choices you make will be difficult, they will have an effect on you in the moment, and will make your journey significantly more difficult, as you cannot avoid these decisions.
It's unfair.
Life is unfair.
I will now break down LISA into pros/cons like the good little reviewer I was born to be.
Pros:
-Great soundtrack, I still listen to a few of the songs on my own time, and each area has it's own little (widdly2)diddly as you walk about and absorb the atmosphere.
-Incredible atmosphere, LISA is hopeless, you will feel hopeless, but that's part of the enjoyment, the comedy given to you in the form of characters and wacky situations help raise your spirits to give you the motivation to continue on regardless.
-Story(?), LISA easily has one of the most dark and inhuman storylines of any game I've ever had the pleasure of playing, it will destroy your sense of being and bring you back to the light only to send you back to hell. It makes you feel things. It's good.
-Combat(?), Although many would say combat was the shortcoming of LISA, I actually found it a bit fun, it works on a basic WASD dial combo system to dial in skills for extra damage. If you were too lazy to learn the combos yourself, you could simply circumvent the dial combos and go straight to the skill menu. This feature was a blessing and a curse, the latter I will explain later.
-Art, The art was nothing special to be honest, but it was definitely really good and the earthy tones really helped convey the tone Dingaling was going for.
Now, onto our cons.
-Difficulty Curve, LISA's main selling point may just be it's downfall. It's hard. This game was incredibly hard in it's beginning stages, albeit it becomes easier as the game goes on, it almost turned me off and has actually turned off many other players from continuing the game. Anyone who buys this needs to understand that you'll need to push past that first crossroads before the game picks up and you can actually fight things.
-Combat(?), LISA's combat is a real crapshoot, you either like it or hate it, or who knows, you might be fine with it, but it definitely wasn't anything revolutionary and ESPECIALLY in the beginning stages it's tedious as hell and can really get frustrating to fight anything. It gets better later on, but as I said, the steep curve of this game turns players off right from the beginning without showing them a light at the end of the tunnel
-Story(?), LISA's story is ♥♥♥♥ed up, and for the most people, hardly relateable. It's really dark and depending on your life experiences you will either become enthralled in it's world or be completely turned off by it's harshness. Really a matter of preference.
-GODDAMN ♥♥♥♥ING CLIFFS, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T
Overall, I rate LISA:The Painful RPG a 8/10, could have been better on the mechanics side of thing, but overall an amazing title and a great addition to anyone's library.

Across all dimensions, the only constant is Darkness! A procedurally generated RPG-roguelike journey across the multiverse!
In One Way Heroics, you take on the role of an intrepid adventurer who must travel across the land and face the Demon Lord before a mysterious darkness engulfs everything.
Darkness always approaches from the left, and with each movement, attack and action you take, the darkness creeps ever closer. Forced to run right, you'll encounter any number of monsters, allies, thieves and shops on your desperate journey to stop the end of everything.
The good news is that you don't just have access to one world. You have access to all of them. Born with the mysterious power to travel to other dimensions, you can choose which dimension you wish to travel to in order to get to the Demon Lord.
Dimensions vary based on their name. One might be full of lush forest landscapes full of adorable animals and cunning thieves, while another might be full of corrupted hellscapes infested with demons. You might find likeminded heroes willing to journey with you, or you might meet no one and be forced to venture into the unknown alone.
Like a dimension you previously visited? Simply input the name at the Dimensional selection screen before you begin your journey. Want to try your luck with a random dimension? Type any word that pops into your head, and watch as One Way Heroics builds you a world based on the name you chose.
Infinite permutations. Infinite worlds. Infinite adventure.

Trials Evolution: Gold Edition is a game where you drive a MOTHER♥♥♥♥IN' DIRT BIKE up ramps and over obstacles, thousands of times, often while grimacing and swearing to yourself that this time, this fault, this checkpoint will be the time you finish against these insurmountable odds.
There are over 120 tracks, ranging from easy, fast tracks, to license tests that are neat tutorials which also unlock a new bike, all the way to Hard and Extreme tracks, which can last upwards of 20 minutes before you finally reach the end, cursing each time you have to retry. A handful of bikes change up the pace a bit as you progress, but by and large the game remains unchanged in its mechanics from start to finish.
That isn't a knock, though, because over time you'll learn various new techniques to help you overcome the ever-increasing challenges of the tracks to become a champion.
A handful of mini-game type tracks, tournaments, and themed tracks keep the game fresh, and striving for Gold (or even Platinum!) medals in tracks will keep you coming back for a long time. In addition, there's a multiplayer mode where you can compete against your friends on a series of tracks to see who gets the best time. It's barebones but fun, and though uPlay is a significant hassle, it's worth it for the zany antics and rush of competition.
Overall, Trials Evolution: Gold Edition is a great game that combines two well-regarded games (Trials HD and Trials Evolution) into a fun package that gives you as much back as you put into it. Some people say there are optimization issues, and indeed on some later tracks the framerate will dip wildly into the teens before climbing back to a playable framerate, but overall it's a good port.
I give it 8.5/10 stars and hope to see future Trials games hitting PC, because I'll be there for the ride.

So I think I've played this game enough at this point to give an honest opinion.
This game sucks.  Let's go through the reasons why.
1.  The graphics - Okay so the graphics aren't terrible, the problem lies in the game engine.  You'll have to force your video card to run at full throttle if you have a modern graphics card.  For whatever reason this game will not trigger full utilization of my graphics cards.  Another huge problem is that textures pop in and out, from blurry to sharp.  Objects will pop as well.  This makes this game very irritating to play since you need to see the things in front of you in order to know how to approach the next jump.  This brings us to our next problem.
2. The camera - I understand that this is a console port, and like every other crappy Ubi console port it suffers.  This was evidenced in the graphics and is also apparent in the view with which the game is presented in.  It's essentially like a 3D version of the NES classic Excitebike where the view is from the side.  However, the viewing angle is schewed a little more toward 70 - 80 degrees.  This is very annoying and does not allow you to complete many of the levels on the first attempt.  Granted the levels are divided into segments via checkpoints which you can "reset" to when you inevitably crash.  Which brings us to...
3.  Level Design - Get ready for some of the most repetitive gameplay ever, with only very small variations on the gas / lean / jump theme.  Some levels have some humor to them, and at the end of every track your guy dies in assorted fashions, but the novelty wears off.  Some of the levels are just plain infuriating, having predetermind events that affect the layout of the course, often with varying results.  Speaking of varying results...
4.  Physics - Or complete lack thereof.  I still can't figure out why your bike sometimes will act as if it has weight to it like a real motorcycle, yet other times its as if it is floating on a single point that refuses to stabilize.  For example, you can land a jump and your bike seems to be planted and you can give it gas and it responds as it should.  Another time you can land off that same jump and your bike is almost uncontrolable and just wants to flip backwards no matter how delicate you apply the gas.  It makes no sense and ruins the game very easily.
5. - Controls - Quite possibly my biggest complaint with this game.  So you control the balance of the bike with gas, brake, and lunge/lean.  I say lunge/lean and not just lean because there is no way for you to gently lean your bike forward.  Any bit of input toward the right results in your rider thrusting his face over the handlebars.  Which interferes with blancing landings and climbing wills since this motion will pull your back wheel off the ground and usually results in an endo.
6. - Uplay - Is a joke.  If you've ever had to use Uplay then you understand.  Whats the point of buying the game on Steam if we're forced to use Uplay?
Save yourself some money and go find an old copy of Motorcross Madness.  That is a much more entertaining game and is over a decade old.  Oh and textures won't pop in and out...

The Developer was very ambitious when making the game, but was forced to release it with a good dose of bugs.
You play as a newly created vampire, and choose one of 7 clans, which will impact how the game plays, some (Malkavian and Nosferatu) more than others. Now you need to maneuver and survive in a secret society of scheming and manipulative power-hungry vampires.
The game is at times funny, dark, serious, silly, scary and the story and dialogue is great. Particularly the early parts of the game. The endgame the missions  will consist of  more  pure "action levels", likely due to the the clock ticking on poor Troika Games. Even so, the result with the unofficial patches is a great adaption of the pen and paper rpg to computer.
(As a side note, it IS possible to finish the game without the unofficial patch... i did, all those years ago. But since the patch exists, theres thankfully really no reason to.)
The graphics are a bit dated, and physics can turn a bit involuntarily funny, but the story and voice acting is great makes up for it.  They really put in the effort there. Do keep saves though, while the patches ironed out most bugs, you could still be unlucky.
At last, if you havent played it and has made the great choice of checking it out, a few tips:
Dont start as Malkavian. They're great for a second play, when you know the overarching plot already, and can catch the truths that leak trough the cracked lenses of the Malkavian's hilarious  madness. You'll miss some in-jokes if its your first playtrough.
Nosferatu, you could start as these, but it changes the game a good bit more than the others,  turning a good bit of it into a stealth game.
The other five are all suited for a first go, some are by nature better talkers some better fighters. Your character will have use of both social and martial skills. XP is gained by completing missions and side missions, so you dont lose out on talking your way past an obstacle. In some cases it might earn you a bonus XP or extra resources.

So...Mafia II? I friend asked me if the game is worth it some time ago, and I decided to reinstall it, play it once again, and since I'm at it, do a Steam-review of it. So yeah, let's start with this, but as usual, I'll start with the BAD things of the game first, to get them out of the way:
First, is that for a open-world game, it's kind of short. I was expecting something as big and long as San Andreas, but it took me about 12-14 hours to finish it. It was indeed a good experience, the story is good (more on that later), but short. It doesn't help that some part of the story is explained in a DLC. I just can't bring myself to buy a damn DLC to see the story, it's lame, and it should never be like this.
Another issue I have with the game, is the first Chapter. You're introduced to the main character in a flashback, but when you finally are in control of the game, you're in a war. You spend most of the game in the city, being a criminal and a gang-member, having a forced tutorial in a war, killing people who look like nazis (I know they're not, but forgot who they where supposed to be, I blame Obama for that) is not the best way to start the story.
The third problem this game has on it, are the controls. At times they feel clunky and weird. I guess the game was made for consoles, rather than PC. They do work most of the time, and you will get used to it, but it still deserves to be mentioned.
Now, let's talk about what the game does well: The story is well set, way better than other open-world games. The game actually looks from the age it's supposed to be, the characters are quite interesting, the town looks mostly alive (excluding weird NPC's doing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stuff, the IA is a bit brain-dead at times), and it's a joy to watch. The game also runs smoothly even on the sh#ttier PC's. Right now, I'm using the back-up PC because the good one kinda blew up to pieces, and it runs over 40 frames per sec without a problem.
As I said before, the story is, being trully honest, quite amazing. It has it's own share of clichés, but for the most part, it's well executed. Infact, the devs knew what they were doing; This game doesn't f#ck arround. It's really violent, like it was back then (not like I lived those days, but dude, I always liked history). The game even has a world record for the game where the word "F#ck" has been used the most, and that's quite an achievement on it's own. It also has mature content arround, for some reason the collectibles are...Porn magazines. Yeah. Not kidding. Now if you see someone who has the 100% Collectible achievement, you know he's a god-damn pervert.
A lot of people talk♥♥♥♥♥♥about the driving mechanics, but personally? I liked them. It actually looks more like the real thing, not like these modern games where a car reaches over 300 km/h in a moment and breaks the laws of physics and matter when it hits something solid. The gameplay though it's questionable. Not gonna say it's bad, but a bit generic. It's a third person shooter with cover mechanics. I'm kind of tired of seeing so many games use them, really...But well, they did try to do it well, and in the most part, they did.
It's not a long game, and it's nowhere close to a master piece, but that doesn't mean that you should stay away from it. Give it a try, you will have fun shooting people in the d#ck. Still, I wouldn't spend 30€ on it, you should wait for a sale, and since the Xmas sales are 2 months away, maybe you should look into it then. 15€ is a good price for it, and for 10€ or less, not buying it will make you look like an #sshole. I would rate this game, but I don't want chinese triads to come here and chop my face off, so I'll leave it with "an Old-school afro / 10". Oh, and there's a "Deluxe" version that costs 10 more euros, that seems to include all the DLC's. The game is entertaining enough as it is, it's up to you to buy them or not.

Hack Slash Loot è un RPG puro, difficile ed estremamente longevo.
Pensato per essere realmente guidato dal fato e in minima parte dall'abilità delle proprie doti di giocatori, si può fare ben poco quando si beve la pozione sbagliata che disincanta tutti i propri oggetti magici, tuttavia ci si può trasformare in una macchina da guerra se le cose girano dalla nostra parte.
Nonostante l'apparente randomicità, il gameplay è del classico RPG per eccellenza, a turni e senza dare vantaggi a nessuno, ne a noi ne ai nemici.
Il gioco parte con personaggi deboli che moriranno senza scampo su tutti i livelli disponibili, poi man mano che moriremo, si sbloccheranno personaggi decisamente più interessanti come l'amazzone, probabilmente il personaggio più facile e potente da usare di tutto il gioco.
Se vi piace il genere puro RPG questo è un must, deve anche interessarvi poco la grafica, o almeno essere abbastanza vecchi da godervi un gioco a 8-bit in tutto il suo disarmante e scarno splendore.
PROS
- Puro RPG
- Immediato e semplice
- È come mangiare le patatine fritte, quando parti non riesci a fermarti
- Nonostante la disarmante semplicità grafica riesce ad essere vario
- Lo stile visuale è coerente e molto consistente
CONS
- Morire contro il mostro di fine quest, dopo 2-3 ore di gioco capita, spesso
- Morire contro un nemico a caso dopo molto impegno capita, spesso
- Frustranti capovolgimenti durante la partita
- Ci stava poter guidare più personaggi nella stessa partita
- Si sente la mancanza di uno story mode più profondo

Hack Slash Loot is great fun. A rougelike-like, dungeon crawling RPG game, with a cutie pixel-art graphics style, and challenging gameplay. It's a turn based game, where each time you move on a tile, you along with everything else in the dungeon takes a turn, and you go through the dungeon completing quests. At the main menu you'll pick a character/class, each which have their own stats and unique style of play (melee, magic, ranged, etc) and depending on the quest, some may be better than others. You also choose the quest you want to play from the main menu, and each has its own story. But everytime you play one of these quests, the dungeon is different, since they're procedurally generated. (Though depending on the quest, they'll follow a certain "blueprint". For instance, a quest that takes place in a large tower will always have a circular shaped map/dungeon). Fun, challenging, and bite sized, HSL is a great way to spend a half an hour or so.

A very well-produced game. The mechanics and levels were clearly put together with a great deal of care. The atmosphere is excellent, and the levels are fun and challenging without being hard just for the sake of being hard.
The game is relatively short, only 2-3 hours on a first play-through, but I honestly prefer that in games these days - when your days are long and you have little time for video games, it's nice to be able to finish one in just a few evenings! A Story About My Uncle doesn't overstay its welcome. It doesn't feel either dragged out or rushed. For people looking for more gameplay, there are quite a few collectibles to give it some replay value if you didn't catch them all the first time through.
Each of the different areas has its own distinct feel and its own mechanic - everything from glow-bushes in the pitch black to stalagtites that fall when you grapple from them. The different biomes are well-realized, with attention to detail. The windmill village, especially, is quite lovely. The mechanics all feel smooth and well-implemented. They aren't necessarily anything extraordinarily innovative, but they feel fresh within the context of the game. It's not just some stale re-hashing of old ideas; everything fits into the game nicely.
The bedtime story vibe of the game is one that resonates with me. It keeps the tone light, even as a couple of the areas are rather foreboding. It moves the game along, keeps you engaged with the narrative, and generally provides an excellent backdrop to the gameplay.
There are a few things that I think could have been done better. The game could have benefited from some more attention to the soundtrack. I'm not saying that the soundtrack was *bad* by any stretch of the imagination, just... the ambient sounds were just that: extremely ambient without having any interesting melodies. I'm a huge sucker for games with a good soundtrack. Additionally, it would have been fun to be able to interact with and speak to the various NPCs. Just having some textual dialogue, even if it wasn't voice acted, would have been neat. It would have given the towns a bit more life.
Overall, however, I definitely recommend this game! I'd certainly buy it again. I don't think I'd pay full price, but if you see it for around $5-7, I'd say you're going to be getting your money's worth.

Now, take this reveiw with a grain of salt, due to my bias verus the newer battlefronts, very much so verus the loot boxes in the newer 'Battlefront 2' (Which is the 5th game in the series, if I remember rightly.)
TL:DR: Great old game, needs a little bit of searching to fix some flaws.

Now, Why would someone get this game?
+ A Class system that leaves no class overpowered verus the others.
+ A Fair amount of modes: Conquest, CTF, Assault for Space maps, Hunt, where you play as a  hunted, Being a Gungun, Wookie, or Ewok to name a few, verus the hunter, Being B2 super battle droids, Magnaguards, or scout troopers, and XL, a PC exclusive mode that pit 64 players per TEAM verus eachother in a deathmatch.
+ NO LOOT BOXES THAT YOU NEED TO BUY TO LEVEL
+ Able to be bought NOW for a 1/6th of the price of the new one.
+ Fairly decent Starfighter controls with a Keyboard and Mouse, which suprised me due to the games age.
+/- Fairly decent Alternate Universe campaign where you mainly play as the clones.
+ Actually makes the Prequels, exlcuding the phantom menace, (And Rogue one, but rogue one was great.) Good.
+ You can mod Maps, units, Modes etc.
+ Multiplayer support is back now.
What about some negatives?
- Some graphic cards will experiance Texture glitchs, but they are fairly simple to fix, See the Steam community and Youtube.
- Bit dated graphics, but, again, easier fix with a Mod.
- Outdated controls for ground units, but as a theme with this reveiw, can be rebinded easily.
My personal Opinion.
Most certianly a great old game to pick up if you want something to play offline or Online, compared to it's modern descendants, whom are infected with the Lootbox and 'Season pass' Culture Syndrome. This game, is the one game, where, you put down $9.99 (Or regional equivalent) and you GET A GAME. *Gasp.* If you are boycotting the new battlefronts, get this game instead. Sure, looks a bit old, controls a little wonky, and the texture issue for a few graphic cards, but once you fix the textures, forgive the graphics a little bit due to age, and rebind controls, this is a solid game to pick up.
9.1/10 is the rating I would give this game, where as I would give the new Battlefront (2015) a 6/10 and Battlefront 2 (2017) a Boycott/10 due to lootboxes.

Whew. This was an experience.
Firstly, I'll get the technical stuff out of the way. For not really being a game, the "gameplay" was alright and handled pretty well. Grabbing and dropping was a little odd, but not a huge problem. At first, it focused mainly on dreams and how nothing makes sense from a distance, then transitioning into amplifying the "sense." I'd enjoy this  a lot more if the ending had a sort of pick-me-up, or a sign of hope. Halfway through I got really depressed and I'm finding that the end was constructed to quickly stop the game instead of wrapping everything up.

A deceptively cute and simple game that you soon realize isn't as kid-friendly as you originally thought.
The game has great writing, features many funny moments, and contains a plethora of unexpected happenings. The game's characters are very unique, and the main character makes an incredibly strong impression for all the wrong reasons. Of course, this doesn't mean the other characters were any less memorable. There's plenty of miscellaneous dialogue to get lost in, and the narration is great.
The game length is decent, and I finished it in eight hours, although it is worth mentioning that I did it in one sitting simply because I found the game so damn compelling. I was pleasantly surprised by the fact that chapter one was not the entire game, as I'd been assuming ever since I forgot the game actually had chapters. At this point the game introduced a new mechanic that in my opinion sadly wasn't used to its full extent (though it was still rather good). That's not saying the game was dragged out too long for them to actually use it enough, it's just that some abilities were one-time use.
Throughout the game you're presented with different interactive puzzles, which serve as nice breaks from the running back and forth. For every puzzle, you have the option to skip them if you so desire, but I personally never did, because they were genuinely good. However, it's worth to mention that one of these puzzles was more of a trial and error game. This is something I realized very early on in the puzzle and it instantly sucked the fun out of it. Still, it was a really small part of the game and is honestly neglectable.
The voice acting is pretty good (especially the narrator's), although the rest of the game's audio is nothing noteworthy. That's okay, though, because the game's focus is its narrative, which it really delivers well on.
In short it's a story full of twists and funny turns, and occasional morbid curiosity. The writing is solid and the game mechanics work well, though there's still some to be desired. Top it off with some good voice acting and you can bunch this together with some of the better point & click adventure games out there. Definitely recommended!

TL DR: Bloodlines is sometimes an amazing game. There's great characters to talk to, and World of Darkness 2004 LA is really fun to explore. However, combat/stealth is never good to begin with, and as time goes by, the game starts having it in more quantity and less quality. Still, because of the reasons I mentioned above, I do think you should really play it. It's nowhere near perfect, but still a very good game.
Vampire - the Masquerade: Bloodlines is an FPS/RPG inspired mostly by Fallout and Deus Ex, and it uses the World of Darkness setting and rulebook in modern Los Angeles. Like in Deus Ex, you have several hubs to explore full of side content, as well as more combat/stealth-oriented areas which sort of let you play your way, like Fallout as well. Also like in Fallout, you get more stat checks in dialogue and unique dialogue to certain character archetypes.
The starting character creation alludes to the amount of difference there is in different characters. Apart from the usual stats/skills/spells, the most important choice you make in character creation is your vampire clan. Each clan has a different combination of spells, some of them unique to that clan, and some of the clans even go further. Nosferatu are visibly deformed and hideous vampires, so you can't be seen by humans, forcing you to stay mostly to the sewers beneath each hub. The Tremere have powerful blood magic, but they have a lower limit to their physical stats. Ventrues can Dominate people in dialogue to do their bidding, but since they're usually aristocrats, they vomit while feeding on homeless people and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. Malkavians are completely insane and so their dialogue is completely different from all the other clans, and can sometimes spoil certain aspects of characters (people usually recommend playing Malk for the first run, and I followed this, but for the previous reason I'd advise against it.) After character creation, you start the game in someone's house, having sex with them, when that someone turns you into a vampire, or "sires" you. The Camarilla, the western vampire organization, punishes this with death for both the Sire and the Childe, but the Prince of LA decides to spare you for you to do his errands. After this you get an optional tutorial and you're good to go in Santa Monica, the first hub.
Bloodlines' first three hubs (out of the four Santa Monica, Downtown LA, Hollywood and Chinatown) are superb. They're all set in the nighttime of LA, where the regular shops close, leaving only businesses such as clubs and hotels open. The game manages to be both mature and humorous at times, and shows a sort of supernatural underworld of Los Angeles which is very well-done. These hubs have really great atmosphere and music, but the characters are what saves Bloodlines from being just an average-good game. Everything about them is good. They're very well-written, voice-acted and animated. The game's writing results in unique and very memorable characters just from the way they talk sometimes. The game uses the Source Engine, so even though animations are sometimes a bit rough, this is compensated by there being very expressive animations. Characters just convey emotions with their faces in a way you rarely see even today! The game provides a lot of choices to play your way in everything (at first), as you can often use both skills and some vampire powers in dialogue. These vampire powers are fueled by blood, and you get blood by, of course, feeding on humans and animals. You can feed on anyone you like but doing so while others are watching breaks the Masquerade, a vampire pact made to hide the existance of the supernatural from the human world. Break the Masquerade five times and you die, though you can get a Masquerade Redemption in some quests. If you're not seen while feeding, or feed off of someone you seduced or a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you paid, you're fine. If you feed on innocents until they die, though, you lose Humanity and are prone to losing control and Frenzying.
These hubs are Masquerade areas, but in combat areas there is no restriction on feeding. You can use both melee and ranged weapons, or your fists, in these areas with no consequence whatsoever. Melee combat is the best for the first half of Bloodlines, and it feels like an amateurish third person brawler where there are no rules to what the staggering animation means, so a staggered foe might be incapacitated for seconds or able to instantly attack you. After the halfway point of the game (About at the end of Hollywood), you start getting ranged weapons that are actually effective, and ranged combat isn't exactly great either, as no gun feels very satisfying to fire. You also have stealth, which is a boring affair of walking crouched and backstabbing people or just right-clicking every 20 seconds to refresh your invisibility while playing Malk or Nosferatu, and I'd say doing a stealth run pretty much requires invisibility, and you can't fully ghost through the game since there are a lot of obligatory bosses. Bloodlines is really at its worst in these combat areas.
From some bits of this review it might be noticeable that the truly great parts of Bloodlines are mostly at its beginning, which is completely true. Bloodlines was rushed to completion, and obviously its latter half suffered greatly. It is the Hollywood Sewers level which marks the point where the game goes down in overall quality. Even though the combat areas so far weren't particularly good, this samey, visually dull level full of the exact same awful enemy for it's first two parts just made me give up and noclip through it. I did this in later levels and I have no regrets. Apart from this the game still left me a sour taste, as the final hub of Chinatown feels very rushed, and almost everything after that is boring combat slogs and HP-bloated bosses, with rarely any non-combat resolutions to anything. Even the Malkavian dialogues start seeming like normal speech but with the different font unique to that clan. There is a really great part before the ending, and the ending I got was satisfying, but the game never reaches the greatness of its first half. And even though there are a lot of fan-made patches to fix the incredible amount of bugs, even when installing Wesp's unofficial patch (the game simply won't run without it on my PC), Bloodlines is still very buggy, with lots of graphical glitches, bugged animations and setpieces, and dialogue audio cues ending too early.
The second half of Bloodlines may not be very good, but its first half is really great despite its sub-par combat. Overall it's a game worth playing, and it's a pity the game didn't have more time in development. If you start getting sick of it by the Hollywood sewers or Hallowbrook Hotel, noclip is your friend.

+ The concept is cute and humerous, seeing a Sloth driving a car... Genious!
+ The gameplay is mildly entertaining. The goal is to drive your car to the end of each stage as fast as possible. Each level tends to have multiple paths to take or tricks to pull off to reduce your time.
+ Visually this game looks wonderful. Very minimalistic in design, but very vibrant colors and lighting, making the world feel  charming.
+ Deceptively challenging. You will have to replay levels again and again in order to shave down your time if you are looking to earn 3 stars. (Adds a lot to replayability)
+ Great upbeat soundtrack
- Some might find the game to be overly difficult as the times required to get 3 stars are extremely tight, and require some fine-tuned driving skills.
- The car mechanics / physics can be frustrating. One small mistake can cost you dearly.

I got this game in the Humble Weeaboo Bundle that was running some time ago. You see, I was thinking "hurr durr all those games have steam cards yay free games for me," without actually considering if they would be fun. Frankly, I didn't expect any of them to be fun for longer than maybe half an hour.
And boy was I wrong.
>>SOUNDS AND MENUS AND PRACTICAL THINGS AND STUFF<<
When I started it up, I was greeted by the typical low-resolution menu screen that reminded me of some fond childhood memories with my mother. I would be playing on the couch with my gameboy, sound on, and after a while my mother would express her annoyence of this sound by imitating them with considerable volume. The sounds that engulfed me from my speakers when I started the game and saw the menu were the kind of sounds my mother would so fondly imitate to me with her loud loving voice.
Already almost teary-eyed I pushed the button on my controller - which works flawlessly with this game - to begin a new adventure.
Again, I saw a screen pop up in front of me which reminded me of home, of my mother. You see, I had to pick a name. And it so happens that my mother gave me my name. Hence, the memories. I felt the tears forming in my eyes again.
Aside from picking a name, I also had to choose a class and several perks. My choice for a class was somewhat limited at first, as I could only choose between two classes. This, however, did not discourage me. For it seemed to me that there would be many opportunities for unlockable characters. And who doesn't love unlockable characters? Gleeful at the prospect of being able to unlock things I picked a class at random, after which I proceeded to put all of my perk slots into extra strength. I would need it.
My heart leapt with excitement as I pushed the button that would initiate my adventure.
Another screen popped up: the final portal that would bring me to the different universe that I had been waiting for. All I had yet to do was choose which universe this would be. A multitude of opportunites (i.e. more or less 7) appeared before my eyes. And once more, childhood memories filled my mind. Of my mother, who would with a kind smile let me pick out my own clothes, and then get mad at me for not being able to pick anything good. Tears streaming from my eyes I went for the option that my mother would have chosen. The randomly generated world.
Another two pushes on the button (one for picking the world, a second one for picking the difficulty), and I finally arrived.
>>STORY<<
I was a hero, and I was greeted by noble king Victor. I was told of a terrible fate to befall these lands. Of darkness, doom, and despair. Of the impending danger that was right behind me. Quite literally. And I would be the one to stop its merciless assault on these former peaceful lands.
And so I embarked on my quest. The darkness ever licking at my heels. Again, quite literally.
I noticed that I also had gained help, in the form of an artificial fairy called Iris. She seemed to be there for all the questions I had, which were none as the blood of heroes had been passed down to me from my mother and hence I did not need any help. I blinked away a tear.
>>GAMEPLAY<<
I rushed through the lands, never resting. Every step I took seemed to take at least 5 minutes. And every step I took seemed to make the many monsters that roamed the lands take one step closer to me as well.
But I couldn't dally and dance with these fiends for long. With every action of mine the darkness crept closer. I knew that it would be my end should it reach me. So I continued, slashing through waves and waves of demons and monsters as fast as I could.
On the way, I met many different innocent people. They would offer me their help in exchange for the money I came across on my journey. It was a sad business they practiced. As much as I would have wanted to, there was no way I could save them from the darkness that was creeping towards us. Merely moments after I had finished bartering with them, I would hear their dying screams coming from behind me. From inside the darkness, where they met an untimely demise. With my money.
>>REPLAY VALUE<<
Ten minutes in my adventure I died. Like my mother.
Nah just kidding, she's still alive and kickin'.
I did die though.
But my death did not discourage me. I had learned from my failures and had become stronger through them. And I knew that I would keep standing up each time I fell down. And I would keep growing stronger, and stronger, and stronger.
And at last, I would make it. I would defeat the big evil boss, and peace would return the world!
But, would it be enough?
There were many other similar worlds. Like EWGHF, or QWUIHNAJ, or HHSJHEUI, or any other world that seemed to have gotten their names from some deity ramming his head on his keyboard several times.
Each and every single one of them needed the help of someone.
And that someone would be me. A hero.
A hero, like my mother.
;_;7

A very well-produced game. The mechanics and levels were clearly put together with a great deal of care. The atmosphere is excellent, and the levels are fun and challenging without being hard just for the sake of being hard.
The game is relatively short, only 2-3 hours on a first play-through, but I honestly prefer that in games these days - when your days are long and you have little time for video games, it's nice to be able to finish one in just a few evenings! A Story About My Uncle doesn't overstay its welcome. It doesn't feel either dragged out or rushed. For people looking for more gameplay, there are quite a few collectibles to give it some replay value if you didn't catch them all the first time through.
Each of the different areas has its own distinct feel and its own mechanic - everything from glow-bushes in the pitch black to stalagtites that fall when you grapple from them. The different biomes are well-realized, with attention to detail. The windmill village, especially, is quite lovely. The mechanics all feel smooth and well-implemented. They aren't necessarily anything extraordinarily innovative, but they feel fresh within the context of the game. It's not just some stale re-hashing of old ideas; everything fits into the game nicely.
The bedtime story vibe of the game is one that resonates with me. It keeps the tone light, even as a couple of the areas are rather foreboding. It moves the game along, keeps you engaged with the narrative, and generally provides an excellent backdrop to the gameplay.
There are a few things that I think could have been done better. The game could have benefited from some more attention to the soundtrack. I'm not saying that the soundtrack was *bad* by any stretch of the imagination, just... the ambient sounds were just that: extremely ambient without having any interesting melodies. I'm a huge sucker for games with a good soundtrack. Additionally, it would have been fun to be able to interact with and speak to the various NPCs. Just having some textual dialogue, even if it wasn't voice acted, would have been neat. It would have given the towns a bit more life.
Overall, however, I definitely recommend this game! I'd certainly buy it again. I don't think I'd pay full price, but if you see it for around $5-7, I'd say you're going to be getting your money's worth.

I REALLY enjoyed this game. Even though i hadn't played 'edna and harvey: the breakout', it was still easy to follow the storyline.

The game has a dark humour to it that you just have to love. If you are the type that can't handle that, you won't enjoy it, but if you like weird/sarcastic/cynical humour, you definitely have the right game!

The gameplay is simple and the story is quite straight-forward, though you can explore a lot and I advise you to do so. Especially some conversations are hilarious and worth listening to. The narrator of your story is quite the sarcastic basterd at times, which is a lot of fun!
The only thing that bothered me was the ending, though I won't tell you anything about it. And there are a lot of: ''what the hell am i supposed to do now!?'' moments in the game. You really have to keep exploring all the options. Though it gave me a lot of frustration.
So in short: a challenging game with a lot of dark humour and funny characters. I definitely recommend it!

The jokes are very dark most of the time, but if you can appreciate dark humor its a great game. The game lasts about 8 hours from start to finish. The only problems I've had with Harvey's New Eyes is a single German translation in the English version (also found occasionally in the Deponia games) and the fact that achievements are bugged and can't be earned even after reaching the requirement, which apparently is a very common problem.
Still, Harvey's New Eyes is a great game and I highly recommend it. The few issues I've had with it don't make a huge impact on the experience given, earning this game 10 Woogies out of 10.

Lisa tells the story of Brad, a broken man, forsaken by hope, who relies on self-medication to forget his haunting past. The setting is a post-apocalyptic wasteland, where women no longer exist and porn magazines replace money. Lust has made monsters of the men that have survived. You will encounter characters that will fight relentlessly or kill themselves before your eyes. Soaked with despair, this world varies from being horrid to hilarious.
Death is ever-present and you can lose your companions permanently or sacrifice parts of yourself to spare their lives. Do you deserve your arm anyway?
The story begins when the protagonist Brad finds an infant girl, and is given the chance to right his wrongs and spare her the pain he suffered. Keeping her isolated, although she represents the future for a world that has none.
Lisa tells an eventful, compelling story that will make you laugh, aggravate you, and quite often leave you disturbed. I enjoyed every moment of it and recommend it to everyone that shares a fascination for games that explore the cruel depths of the human mind.

This is more of a first impressions than a full review, but to be honest, I found the first 2.3 hours very dull indeed, and I do not wish to press forward. I don't want it to seem like I'm being unfair though, so after the first 2 hours, here's what I did like about it:
PROS:
- Good Story.
If you're a fan of dark humor, (like I am), then this game shall not dissappoint. It starts off very serious, conveying the story of a boy, our protagonist, living with his abusive father, until that man eventually grows up in an post-apocalyptic world where all women are dead. He then finds a baby, and not only that, but a female one. This isn't really spoilers as this is all in the intro sequence, and I won't go into any more detail than that, but rest assured that it comes together nicely.
- Characters Are Either Human or Over-The-Top.
Brad Armstrong is the protagonist, a very human main character, surrounded by very inhuman side characters, whose personalities are so ridiculous to become laughable. This isn't really a problem though, as the characters are specifically supposed to be over the top, and it creates an interesting contrast between Brad and the world around him.
-Fantastic Atmosphere.
I love the post-apocalyptic feel in this game. Unlike some post-apocalypse games *cough*Fallout 3*cough* it realizes that a post-apocalypse needs to be subtle. It has a good art style, fitting of the game's tone, and the people around it all have either broken down in insanity, adjusted well (this is the minority), or seem to have this obstinate refusal to admit that an apocalypse even happened.
What you must now ask yourself is "Is that enough?" Because here's where things get bad.
CONS:
- Gameplay is Tedious and Frustrating.
This is what turned me off to the game, after the tutorial level is over, you are thrown into the overworld with absolutely no direction or indication of what makes the game move forward. I'd say it was metroidvania if it was actually fun. After an hour or so of backtracking, I did eventually find out what I was supposed to do through sheer force of will. But then things got even worse. The game design is purposefully unfair to hammer home the sense of the whole world being against you, but it does its job too well. I finally gave up during a section where you're supposed to acquire an item being guarded by an unfair boss battle (whose weakness is never revealed to you btw) that lurks miles away from the nearest checkpoint and on the opposite end of a random-encounter-o-rama. A great, simple and entertaing Rogue-like rpg with a twist.
This games offers engaging sessions of rogue-like adventuring , while being able to persistently unlock new features such as classes, perks and more. While its gameplay mechanics are pretty simple, there are many combinations of randomly-generated equipment, skills and events for you character. Each class is a bit different in terms of gameplay so you'll probably be wanting to try out every available combination of class+perks more than once. The gameplay gets repetitive after a while so I doubt anyone would be playing it 24/7 nonstop, but nevertheless it's a good experience for its price.
One of the few features that caught my eye was a 'Daily Online Challenge' or 'Campaign Dimensions'. Each day the seed is generated for a world where everyone who plays a game can join. While it's impossible to interact directly with other players you can encounter the ghosts of defeated players and read the recent chat logs of other adventurers, how much time they have spent, who killed them and what items they have obtained in this world.
Same with the 'online' adventures, new adventures with different conditions are also generated daily. E.g. The ones where you can recruit a powerful ally, or a world covered in constant darkness, limiting your vision.
9/10 will play again.

One Way Heroics is an excellent game, let alone for the price.
I found it to have one of the smoothest learning curves for rogue-lites/likes. So you can make progress and beat it on an easy difficult consistently with a little practice. And if you can't you can either change your seed for a fresh run, OR practice your current seed and learn where the helpful locations/items are to progress further each time, or maybe store items for that leg up on the next run.
The classes all have a good variety in their bonuses, and while I found the swordsman and Hero easy to make overpowered there's plenty of success and strategy to be had with other classes. The perk system also helps you further optimize or offset weaknesses.
The game even accomdates further in that you can beat the demon lord in a quick 30 minute journey or invest in a 3-5 hour hike to the end of the world. You can even save and come back to journey after a break (or a series of poor decisions).
My rather nitpicky complaint is that the humor is a little immature/pervy, but overall harmless. And that I feel ultimately this game doesn't have quite the staying power of say Binding of Issac or FTL.  This is primarily due to the weapons all feeling very same-y, and there being little  mechanical skill in this game (i.e. if you take your time you should never input an unintended command). The music is also not quite as good as those other games.
That said this game scratches a similiar but different itch from those games and even if you only get 20 hours out of the game they will be 20 hours you won't regret, and stuff like daily events and the hardest difficulties could potentially get you many more past that.

There's actually a lot to like about KAG. It's not revolutionary, with every mechanic you see being something you've seen many times before, but it's all combined in a way that offers a good theme and potentially a fair amount of fun.
But, the servers ARE mostly empty. And the game doesn't necessarily offer good balance of play (It's much faster to destroy than build, and very easy to get past most enemy fortifications, making for a generally unsatisfying game for Builders, one of the game's 3 classes). It's a game that's hard to be good at, that mostly only has a dedicated playerbase left, meaning it's a VERY unfriendly environment for newbies.
It's a good-enough game, and I've enjoyed it intermittently over the years. But it's past it's prime, and for a multiplayer game of this particular kind? That's actually a pretty serious issue.

Fast enough to sail right into people, buildings, and sharks and do heavy damage.

If you enjoy puzzle games with a bit of mathematical thinking, you will like Divide By Sheep.  You must move groups of sheep around platforms and hazards in order to get the exact # required for the level.  Be warned, this game was clearly designed for a mobile platform due to mandatory "click & drag" controls and "Click here to Rate us 5 Stars!" type messages.  However, it is still fun if you enjoy this genre, otherwise, it can get boring and frustrating if you want more action.  Recommended if on sale.
PROS
+ Cute graphics and sound
+ Puzzles can be solved multiple ways
+ Math fans will enjoy the calculative gameplay
+ Lots of different puzzle concepts (half sheep, hungry wolves, etc.)
CONS
- Clearly designed for mobile ("Click here to Rate!")
- Click & Drag controls can be irritating
- Some concepts not clear (halving sheep was confusing at first)
- Difficult levels can get frustrating
